title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Kitchen Table Home Game. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Kitchen Table Home Game
options.lineage: Friday-night home games: fold-out felt on the kitchen table, a tin of clay chips, a pencil ledger
options.thesis: A friend's kitchen table at 22:00: faces around a fold-out felt, one lamp lighting whoever has to act.
options.viewport: Walnut ground; a rounded-square felt topper centre with board cards and the pot as a real chip pile; nine seats are live camera tiles set around it like chairs; blind clock strip at the top; your action bar docked bottom; ledger in a side drawer.
options.risk: Warm brown and teal can tip into cosy pastiche if the controls are not crisp, standard and fast.

raised.raise: Lamp amber is the only saturated colour on controls, and it appears only on what you can do right now.
Your decision timer and the blind level are drawn as exact-length bars: length is time left, nothing decorative.
Hierarchy by scale alone: the pot and the amount to call set huge, everything else small and quiet.

options.label: Poker Broadcast
options.lineage: televised poker: hole-card cams, player plates, lower-third graphics
options.thesis: Your game night produced like a TV final table: every face is a camera feed with a broadcast player plate.
options.viewport: Felt-free dark stage; seats are framed camera feeds with name/stack plates; pot and board in a central graphics package; action bar as a lower third.
options.risk: The most familiar route for a poker product with video; dark broadcast navy is close to the category's night-mode default.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.thesis: Soft cards on a warm ground, one saturated colour only where you can press.
options.viewport: Table drawn as a soft rounded card on a warm ground, seats as white player cards, big friendly action buttons.
options.case: Holds clarity (your options are the only bright thing) but loses audience identification: it reads as an app, not a poker night.
options.risk: Generic: could be any consumer app with cards on it.

options.label: Dance Score
options.thesis: Action as a vertical score where length is exact duration.
options.viewport: Hand history as a rising score.
options.case: Players do not identify with notation; the table becomes a diagram.
options.kept: Time drawn as exact length: turn timer and blind level as measured bars.

options.label: Midnight Transit Map
options.thesis: Seats as stations, the pot as the interchange.
options.viewport: Action routed along coloured lines into the pot.
options.case: Metaphor costs clarity and nobody at a home game thinks in lines.
options.kept: The chosen line burns brightest: only the acting seat is lit.
options.risk: Costume of a map on a working screen.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: Preflop to river as fixed-scale plates on one baseline.
options.viewport: Board streets as five aligned plates.
options.case: Cream-and-serif reading of a card game; weak identification.
options.kept: Five board slots always drawn at fixed scale on one baseline, empty ones included.

options.label: Convention Catalog
options.thesis: Packed stamp-size cells marked in biro.
options.case: Density fights faces; loses both axes.
options.kept: Hand-marked state: folded seats visibly struck, not just dimmed.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: Numbers as giant glyphs that change weight with value.
options.viewport: Pot as a giant morphing numeral.
options.case: Clever but cold; friends do not see a game night.
options.kept: Hierarchy by scale contrast: pot and call amount huge, labels tiny.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The green felt oval on a dark room, PokerNow-style, executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Oval table centre, seat boxes around the rim, action buttons bottom right.
